summary: Profile infrastructure package. Defines the runtime-checkable ProfileProtocol (to_handler_kwargs) and its storage refinement StorageProfileProtocol (adds get_connection_url), plus StorageProfileSpec, a frozen ProfileSpec subclass carrying storage metadata (sdk_package, handler_module/handler_class, streaming/multipart/read_only flags, default_auth, supported_auth, implemented). The package __init__ eagerly exposes only the stdlib-only protocols and lazily resolves the spec and loader names, raising MissingExtraError naming [http] when those dependencies are absent.
key_classes: ProfileProtocol — runtime-checkable base contract: to_handler_kwargs() -> dict[str, Any] of SDK-ready config (no credentials)
StorageProfileProtocol — storage refinement adding get_connection_url() for diagnostics/logging; the type the facade, registry and resolve_storage accept/return

StorageProfileSpec — frozen kw_only dataclass extending mountainash_settings ProfileSpec with storage metadata: sdk_package, handler_module, handler_class, supports_streaming, supports_multipart, read_only, default_auth, supported_auth, implemented
key_functions: __getattr__(name) — PEP 562 lazy loader for spec/loader names; converts ImportError into MissingExtraError for the [http] extra
extension_points: Implement ProfileProtocol/StorageProfileProtocol structurally (runtime_checkable) to supply a custom profile to StorageFacade or get_storage_backend
Declare a StorageProfileSpec as a Profile subclass's __spec__ and decorate with settings.storage.registry.register to add a provider profile
ProfileProtocol is documented as the base for future messaging/connection profile families (settings/messaging/ is a docstring-only placeholder)
lifecycle_notes: profile_protocol.py is stdlib-only and importable on a base install; profile_spec.py imports mountainash_auth_client and mountainash_settings and therefore needs [http]

Spec and loader names are resolved lazily on attribute access; the root package re-exports ProfileProtocol, StorageProfileProtocol, resolve_storage, StorageProfilesSettings, StorageProfileBlock and AuthBlock through its own lazy table
StorageProfileSpec.implemented must equal whether a backend is registered for spec.provider_type (pinned by a drift test)
documentation_hooks: Profile + auth separation: what a storage profile is and why it never carries credentials
Typing contract: StorageProfileProtocol exposes only to_handler_kwargs() and get_connection_url(); narrow to a concrete class to read fields
Reference table of StorageProfileSpec metadata fields and their meaning
Extras matrix: which settings names work on a base install vs need [http]
examples: examples/storage_profiles/example.py — inspects a StorageProfileSpec (parameters, supported_auth) obtained via the registry
risks: StorageProfileSpec's docstring documents every extra field except 'implemented', which is the field the registry drift test treats as the single source of truth

handler_module/handler_class are descriptive metadata only: backend dispatch goes through storage.registry.register_storage_backend, so these strings can name non-existent modules (e.g. storage.backends.gcs/azure/ftp/smb/github) without any failure
profile_spec.py places its explanatory docstring after the imports, so it is not the module __doc__
open_questions: Should handler_module/handler_class be validated against, or derived from, the backend registry, or removed as redundant metadata?
Is ParameterSpec (re-exported from mountainash_settings) intended to be part of this package's public settings surface?

evidence.detail: Root __all__ and _LAZY export ProfileProtocol, StorageProfileProtocol, resolve_storage, StorageProfilesSettings, StorageProfileBlock, AuthBlock from .settings
StorageProfileSpec dataclass fields including implemented: bool = True
